items.title: 52031_Kenny Clarke oral history interview
items.q: And our best trumpet player, Jimmy Brown, he died in a concentration camp.

ctx.x: Which some of them didn't come back, you know, because the war caught them there. And our best trumpet player, Jimmy Brown, he died in a concentration camp. And another, Jimmy Allen, he was a tenor player, he came back in 1938, just before the war started. And I was working at the Savoy Ballroom with Teddy Hill, and I saw Jimmy walk in, and I said, "Hey, Jimmy. My God." He said, "We just got back from Japan." I said, "Oh, wonderful." And there was a Japanese restaurant just next to the Savoy Ballroom, and he…
But Kenny, what -- the other guy stayed?
